questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: English speaking country, great school and fun country to visit

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. The advisors from UBC were very helpful and UBC's website was also informative

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive assistance upon arrival

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of residences you can apply for on campus. They offer both studio- and shared apartments

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There are unequipped kitchens in all of the residences. Meal plans are offered, however, they seem to mostly be used by first years. Most people either cook or eat out / order takeaway

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend to live on campus, as you will live where a lot happens. Walter Gage, Fairview Crescent and "the houses of the ones belonging to the saltwater" are typical residences, where the latter is newly build and primarily contains studio apartments, and the two former are older and typically contain shared apartments 

You should be aware that kitchens are unequipped, so you will either need to purchase some stuff or borrow from roommates. There is also no bedding, etc. in the units.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Registration is based on two rounds of first come, first serve. In the first round you can apply for 6 credits and you can apply for the rest in the second round.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I received multiple emails from the UBC advisors prior to registration opened and also emailed with them to trouble shoot some stuff during the registration process. Overall they were very helpful!

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was able to get most of the classes I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be ready to register right when the period opens. Some classes are pretty limited in availability, so they might fill up quickly.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were around the same difficulty as we are used to at UCPH, however, you have quite a few more courses, so there is generally more to read

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A lot of my courses had a more lecture style format, however, there are also seminar courses, which are more alike what we are used to from UCPH

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1) Real Estate Transactions
2) Conflict of Laws
3) Mass Torts and Class Actions
4) Labour Law
5) IP-Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Mass Torts and Class Actions was exciting as you get taught how class actions work and look at some of their huge class action tort cases. IP-Law was also amazing, mostly because of the teacher, John Festinger, I would recommend any course with him

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I do not think I had any unexpected costs. I think my costs were pretty clear prior to arrival

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Most things are more expensive in Canada, especially phone plans and groceries. Eating out is not that much more expensive than cooking, and not too expensive compared to Danish prices

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: UBC offers a lot of social actives, including clubs, sports games, etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend attending a university sports game! It is a super fun thing to experience

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore the different areas of town, Granville Island, Stanley Park, etc. You can also take a trip to Vancouver Island

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it pretty easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Don't be too shy - just say "hello" - most Canadians are very nice!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I don't think any cultural differences were particularly challenging

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How nice and approachable everyone is

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Bring an umbrella - it rains a lot
2) Make sure to soak in as many experiences as possible - time flies
3) Use CAN's for exams (= Condensed Annotated Notes from former students)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read up on ideas for trips and sights in and around the city, so you can get inspired for what you want to experience during weekends and breaks - some trips might require a (somewhat early) booking in advance

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making new friends during the term to travel the country with

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I found it hard to see the big picture in some of my courses, because you don't know the basics of Canadian law and society that the Canadian students do

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
